input: Review contract etimad-it and route it.

checks.why: c15: the contractor's duty covers any non-public information and 'يسري هذا الالتزام طوال مدة العقد وبعد إنهاء أو انتهاء العقد' with no end date or trade-secret limit (one-way on the contractor, but the rule is direction-neutral).
c26: the contractor may not assign the contract or part of it, even by merger, without approval of the entity and MoF; subcontracting also needs approval (c23).
c7: fixed term (length is a placeholder) with no renewal; extensions (c71) only for listed causes.

c15-c17: need-to-know use, no disclosure to third parties without the entity's prior consent, immediate breach notice with affected persons, deletion/return at the end, NCA cybersecurity controls; nothing lets the contractor store or move data freely.
c7: Saudi law; c8: Saudi Administrative Courts; the optional arbitration clause (c31) is SCCA seated [Riyadh] under Saudi law.
Only the contractor indemnifies (third-party IP claims c21, losses c42, safety c45); the entity gives no indemnity.
No interest or late-payment charge on the entity anywhere; the only percentages are penalties on the contractor.
c18: all IP delivered under the contract 'ستؤول إلى الجهة الحكومية وستصبح مملوكة ملكًا حصريًّا'; pre-existing works stay with the contractor under a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable licence.
c10: Arabic is the approved language and 'يكون النص الوارد باللغة العربية هو المعتمد' in any conflict.
No exclusivity or non-compete binds the entity; c44 lets it use other contractors.

Payment runs 10 working days (representative) + 15 working days (entity) + up to 45 days (MoF) after the invoice (c87-c88); advance payment is optional, bounded '(لا تزيد عن 10%)' and backed by a bank guarantee (c86).
c81: the entity may terminate 'إذا اقتضت المصلحة العامة ذلك', effective 30 days after notice, paying only for accepted work/materials (c84); the contractor has no convenience right.

No clause caps or limits either party's liability: contractor liability is open-ended (c42) and the contractor may claim compensation from the entity in the Administrative Court (c29, c92); the penalty ceiling (c94) is 'دون الإخلال بحق الجهة الحكومية في أي تعويض'. Whether read as a missing LoL clause or as our uncapped liability, it escalates.

notes: Customer = the government entity (الطرف الأول, buyer); the contractor is the supplier. MoF/Etimad 2020 unified IT template under Saudi law. LIAB-CAP is out of scope: no cap exists for either party, and whether that is a LIAB-CAP finding (our liability uncapped) or just a missing LoL clause (the missing-liab-en-01 convention) is a labelling call; the route is escalate under either reading. Placeholders (term, advance %, penalty %, arbitration seat) do not change any labelled rule.

input: Review contract expro-it and route it.

checks.why: Confidentiality runs for the term and 'وبعد إنهاء أو انتهاء' with no end date and no trade-secret limit (framework c33, purchase-order terms c102); binds the contractor.
Contractor may not assign the framework or a purchase order (even via merger or acquisition) without consent of EXPRO / the entity and the Ministry of Finance (c39, c121).
Initial term one year from 2022/10/09 (c18); an extension 'يجوز إضافة مدة' is discretionary and capped by the regulations (c19); nothing renews automatically.

Contractor may use data only as needed, may not disclose to third parties without prior consent, must report any breach immediately with affected persons, delete/return data at the end, and follow NCA cybersecurity controls (c33, c34, c102, c103).
Governed by the Government Tenders and Procurement Law and the laws in force in Saudi Arabia; Saudi administrative courts decide disputes (c44, c138).
Only the contractor indemnifies: general indemnity to the government entity (c122) and IP third-party claims (c37, c106); the government side gives no indemnity.
No late-payment charge on the government side; the only percentage charges are delay penalties on the contractor (1% per day, capped at 6%, c132).

Pre-existing IP stays with the contractor under a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable licence; all IP delivered (outputs, documents, data, reports) vests exclusively in the government side (c35, c104).
Arabic is the approved language and the Arabic text prevails over any foreign-language version (c29).
'عدم الحصرية': the contractor is not the exclusive supplier and beneficiary entities are not obliged to order from it (c27).
Entity approves the invoice and sends the payment order within 15 working days, MoF pays within 45 days of receiving it (c129); no advance payment anywhere.
EXPRO may end the framework and the entity may end a purchase order for public interest, effective 30 days after notice (c41, c127); framework term is 1 year (c18).
No limitation-of-liability clause in the main document or the General Conditions: contractor liability is unlimited (c122) and only delay penalties are capped (c132).

notes: Customer is the government side: EXPRO signs on behalf of government entities, which buy under purchase orders governed by Annex 2 (General Conditions); the supplier is 'المتعاقد'. LIAB-CAP is out of scope: there is no liability clause to judge (nobody is capped), and the missing clause is what drives the escalate route. OCR noise (page headers, stray Latin, lost sentence starts) decides no labelled rule.

input: Review contract edgar-lucid-mof and route it.

checks.why: The only liability limit is the mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages in 18(j); there is no monetary cap, so the Purchaser's liability (incl. the 50,000-vehicle Minimum Quantity commitment) is uncapped.

Purchaser may terminate only for insolvency, non-supply, change of control (15(b)), breach or force majeure; no termination for convenience on a Term running to the 10th anniversary of the first Purchase Order.
18(e)(i): neither Party may assign without the other Party's written approval.
Clause 3: fixed Term until the tenth anniversary of the first Purchase Order; no renewal mechanism.
18(f): Seller may not disclose Purchaser/Beneficiary information without approval, must notify any breach immediately and delete data on termination; 5(a)(xi) Kingdom cybersecurity requirements.
17(a) laws of the Kingdom; 17(b)(ii) disputes finally settled by the competent court in the Kingdom.
Clause 12 is a one-way Seller indemnity in favour of the Purchaser and Beneficiaries; the Purchaser gives no indemnity.
No late-payment interest or charges anywhere; clause 8 only sets invoicing and payment periods.
Clause 9: each Party retains its own IP; vehicles are sold outright and Purchaser data must be returned or deleted (18(f)(iv)).
18(g): prepared in Arabic and English; 'the Arabic version shall prevail'.
No exclusivity binding the Purchaser; it has a Minimum Quantity purchase commitment but no restriction on buying elsewhere.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: nothing caps the Purchaser's liability.

notes: Customer = Government of KSA (Ministry of Finance), the Purchaser; Lucid L.L.C. is Seller. PAY-TERMS out of scope (advance-payment share and payment days redacted [***] in 8.1); CONF-TERM out of scope (18(f) confidentiality is perpetual but binds only the Seller, in our favour: literal hint vs substance). 7.1 Price and 14(c) are omitted from the filing; the route does not depend on them.

input: Review contract edgar-aramco-po and route it.

checks.why: Para 25 limits only the Vendor's liability for Buyer property (US$ [blank] per occurrence, otherwise insurance limits); nothing caps Saudi Aramco's liability, so the cap is one-sided and our liability uncapped.
Para 2: the Order may not be assigned or subcontracted by Vendor (beyond a value threshold left blank) without Buyer's prior written consent.
One-off purchase order; no term or renewal provision.
Para 1: laws of the Kingdom; arbitration under the Saudi Arbitration Law seated at the SCCA in Riyadh.
Buyer gives no indemnity; Vendor indemnifies for IP infringement (para 21), injury/property (para 25) and tax withholding.
No interest or late charges on the Buyer; the only charges run against the Vendor (late-invoice processing costs).
Para 23: Buyer's Data stays Buyer's; designs, drawings and inventions developed for the Order become Buyer's property.
No exclusivity or non-compete binding Saudi Aramco.
Para 17: Buyer pays 'promptly after delivery' and upon receipt and acceptance of the invoice; no prepayment and no fixed period shorter than 30 days.

Para 14: 'Buyer may cancel all or any part of this Order for its convenience' by electronic notice, paying unavoidable costs plus reasonable profit capped at the Order price; Vendor has no such right.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: only the Vendor's liability is limited.

notes: Customer = Saudi Aramco (Buyer); OMS is Vendor. Aramco's own paper, so nearly every rule favours us; LIAB-CAP is still a finding because only the Vendor's liability is limited. PAY-TERMS no_finding is a deliberate decision ('promptly after delivery' plus invoice acceptance, no prepayment). Many values are blank in the filing (cap amount, warranty periods, assignment threshold); CONF-TERM (para 22 missing from the filing), DATA-PROT (silent) and LANG-PREC (English only, Arabic translation on request, no precedence clause) left out of scope.

input: Review contract cuad-americasshoppingmall and route it.

checks.why: c60 'Assignment' only says the Agreement binds 'successors and assigns' with no consent requirement, so HDI may assign freely.
c24 renews for one-year periods 'unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice': notice window over 60 days.

c65 makes Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 survive two years but omits Section 8 (Confidentiality), so it ends at termination, or if read as unlimited has no trade-secret limit: outside 3-7 years either way.

c37: for the auto-renewing term 'the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet' for its own or similar products, and HDI gets exclusive use of the Deerskin brand for a web site.
No indemnity clause anywhere in the contract; we give none.
No late-payment interest or charge anywhere.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
c20: payments 'due monthly within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar month'; no prepayment.

One-year term renewing yearly (c24) with either party able to end it on 90 days' notice; no term over 12 months and no supplier-only right (the Company's c26 Termination Payment is owed only if trailing net sales exceed $800,000).
No limitation-of-liability clause at all (CUAD's Cap On Liability span is the c26 Termination Payment, not a cap).

notes: Customer = The Deerskin Companies ('Company'); HDI builds and hosts the site for 30% of net sales. CUAD says Cap On Liability = Yes but its span is the c26 termination payment; the text has no cap, so LIAB-CAP is out of scope and the missing cap is tested by route=escalate. IP-OWN (silent on who owns the site HDI builds) and DATA-PROT left out as undecidable.

input: Review contract cuad-corio and route it.

checks.why: c64: Developments Corio creates are owned by Commerce One if it supports them 'on an ongoing basis', with no licence back, and c65 leaves ownership of Corio's Software enhancements 'to be negotiated'.
c83: 'License Fees: Due upon Software Acceptance' and the MarketSite access fee is due on acceptance and each annual anniversary in advance: payment due in fewer than 30 days.
Initial term is five years (c53) and c54 allows termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency: no customer convenience right on a term over 12 months.
c67: no assignment without consent, except either party on a merger or sale of substantially all related assets (not to a direct competitor): Commerce One cannot assign freely.
c53: renews for one-year periods unless either party gives 30 days' notice: within the required position.
The only indemnity is Commerce One's IP-infringement indemnity of Corio (c48); we give none.
No late-payment interest or charge.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.

c50 caps 'EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY' at amounts paid by Corio in the prior twelve months (for the transaction concerned); mutual, and the only carve-out is Section 8, Commerce One's IP indemnity to us.
All licences are nonexclusive and nothing bars Corio from competitors; the no-contact covenant in c17 binds Commerce One.
Mutual 12-month cap (c50) and governing-law/arbitration clause (c69) present; major findings TERM-CONV, PAY-TERMS and IP-OWN, nothing critical.

notes: Customer = Corio, the fee-paying licensee of Commerce One's software (Recital B, s.2.1); it also resells and co-markets, so not pure buyer paper. '[*]' redactions cover fee amounts only. CONF-TERM left out (substance is in a separate NDA not included); DATA-PROT left out.

input: Review contract cuad-vitalibis and route it.

checks.why: c54: successive one-year renewals unless notice 'at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration': notice window over 60 days.
c30: late payments 'accrue interest ... at the rate of one percent (I%) per month'.

c35: 'NOT A WORK-FOR-HIRE AGREEMENT'; all software, data and content Votocast develops (incl. the branded apps and customisations) stay Votocast's, Licensee assigns any rights, and the c7 licence is access during the term only.
c49 caps only 'VOTOCAST'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY' and c48 excludes its liability for data theft, while Licensee's liability and indemnities are uncapped: one-sided cap.
The Exhibit D SOW form makes SOW fees 'due and payable within fifteen (15) days' of invoice (c138) and implementation fees are 'paid in advance' (c88, currently $0); main terms in c30 are 30 days.
c67: consent required, with a carve-out only for an acquirer of substantially all relevant assets (either party) and subcontracting where Votocast stays responsible.
c51: obligations 'shall survive for three (3) years after expiration or termination'.
Indemnities are mutual and for third-party actions: Licensee for its negligence and content (c43, c26), Votocast for its negligence and materials (c44).
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
c72: 'This Agreement is non-exclusive'; each party is free to deal with competitors.
c54: 'Licensee can terminate Agreement with at least one hundred eighty (180) days written notice with no further obligation'; customer-only right on a one-year term, so the hint is not met.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: supplier-only cap.

notes: Customer = Vitalibis ('Licensee'); supplier = Votocast. Exhibit D is a blank SOW form, but its 15-day payment term is part of the agreed exhibits (c10). DATA-PROT left out: c14 gives commercially reasonable privacy efforts and 3 business days' notice before access/disclosure, but no location limits or breach notice; the hint does not cleanly decide it.

input: Review contract cuad-xacct and route it.

checks.why: c27 limits only 'XACCT'S SOLE LIABILITY' (12 months of support fees) and c28 excludes only XACCT's consequential damages; nothing caps Licensee's liability: one-sided cap.
c21: renews for one-year terms unless Licensee gives notice thirty (30) days before the anniversary: within the required position.
No indemnity in the document.
No late-payment interest or charge.
Support-only agreement with no ownership terms; no customer data or bespoke deliverables go to XACCT.
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
No exclusivity or non-compete.
c9: 'Fees shall be payable within thirty (30) days of invoice'; no prepayment stated.
One-year term (c21); neither party has a convenience right (XACCT's c22 rights are for non-payment, breach or product withdrawal) and the term is not over 12 months.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: supplier-only cap.

notes: Draft 'DRAFT (Americas) 1/12/00' with blank date and licensee; customer = Licensee. The End User License Agreement it incorporates by reference, and Attachment 1, are not included and may hold Licensee's own cap, confidentiality and assignment terms, so CONF-TERM, ASSIGN and DATA-PROT are left out; labels judge this document as given.

input: Review contract cuad-blackstone and route it.

checks.why: c3: 'shall automatically renew for successive additional three-year terms': renewal term over 12 months.
c24(c): Section 13 (Confidentiality) survives termination with no time limit and no trade-secret limit: perpetual.

c8: Client indemnifies Agent for 'any loss, liability, claim (whether with or without basis in fact or law)' arising from Agent's duties, incl. costs of enforcing the Agreement; Agent gives no indemnity back.
c20: 'Delinquent payments are subject to a late payment charge of one and one half percent (1.5%) per month'.

c10: 'Any liability of Agent will be limited in the aggregate' to 24 times the monthly administrative fee, and c9 excuses Agent absent gross negligence; Client's liability, incl. the c8 indemnity, is uncapped: one-sided cap.

Three-year renewing term (c3); Client may terminate only for Agent default or insolvency (c13), and any other termination by Client costs 12, 9 or 6 times the average monthly invoice (c14): no penalty-free convenience right.
c24(d): consent required, except Agent may assign to an affiliate or a successor by merger or asset sale and gives notice of the successor: the playbook fallback.
No clause gives Agent the Client's data or any deliverables; on termination Client instructs the disposition of records (c14).
English-only contract; no bilingual text.
No exclusivity or non-compete; Exhibit C even contemplates co-transfer agents (c54).
Critical LIAB-CAP finding: Agent-only cap.

notes: Customer = the Fund ('Client'); supplier = Mellon ('Agent'). PAY-TERMS left out: invoices are net 30 (c20), but postage must be prefunded a business day before each mailing and fees fall due immediately on termination (c14); whether pass-through prefunding trips the rule needs a labelling decision. DATA-PROT left out.

input: Review contract cuad-ofg and route it.

checks.why: c5: renews for twelve months unless Customer objects 'within a period of three (3) months following the Renewal Notice' sent 12 months before expiry: notice window over 60 days.

c40 sets no duration and the c59 survival list ('Articles 5, 8, 9, 0, and 17') has a broken reference, so confidentiality either ends at termination or runs with no limit: outside 3-7 years either way.

c34: Customer indemnifies Metavante for third-party claims 'based on Customer's use of the Services to support its operations' while Metavante covers only US IP infringement; c121 adds 'any and all loss, liability, claims, costs, and expenses' of SecureCode participation.
c18: unpaid charges 'shall be subject to annual interest at the prevailing U.S. prime rate'; c13 charges for unfunded settlement at the Federal Reserve overnight rate.
c23: 'during the Term, Metavante shall be Customer's sole and exclusive provider' of the Integrated Banking Solution, a term running to November 2014.
c18: 'Customer shall pay the Monthly Base Fee in advance on the first day of the calendar month'; c6 also requires data tapes and termination assistance to be paid in advance.

c26: Customer may terminate for convenience only on six months' notice plus a Termination Fee 'equal to the Estimated Remaining Value' (all remaining fees) on a term to November 2014, while Metavante may withdraw services on 90 days' notice (c22).
English-only contract; no bilingual text (bilingual customer statements in c93 are deliverables, not the contract).

notes: Customer = Oriental Financial Group; supplier = Metavante. Section 9.3 (c30, the likely damages cap) and the fee schedules are redacted, so LIAB-CAP and the route are left out: the route is negotiate or escalate depending on 9.3 (visible text has only a Metavante-only cap on Professional Services, c12). IP-OWN (enhancement schedule redacted), ASSIGN (Metavante 'may freely assign' but only on merger, reorganisation or to a successor) and DATA-PROT left out.

input: Review contract claudette-zoom and route it.

checks.why: Customer indemnifies Zoom for any third-party claims 'arising from Your use of the Services'; Zoom gives no indemnity in return.
'Zoom may collect interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the highest amount permitted by law' on late amounts.

Zoom-only exclusion of indirect damages and cap at fees paid in the prior 12 months, plus 'Under no circumstances will Zoom be liable' for Content/data (all ltd2); the customer's liability, including its c26 indemnity, is uncapped.
Zoom charges the customer's card for each subscription term in advance; on cancellation there is no refund 'for any service already paid for' (full prepayment, no 30-day term).
Renewal only if the Order Form provides, with 30 days' non-renewal notice (c17); the customer may cancel at any time and is not billed for further terms (c14).
c20: mutual confidentiality lasts five (5) years from disclosure, inside the 3-7 year range.
c9: 'You retain copyright and any other rights You already hold in Content'; Zoom owns only its Services and marks (c18).
Only a use restriction (no building a competing product with the Services, c9); no exclusivity binding the customer.
Critical LIAB-CAP finding (supplier-only cap, customer uncapped).

notes: Customer = the subscriber (us); Zoom Video Communications is supplier. The CLAUDETTE ter2 spans (c17: terminate for any non-compliance and keep fees; c21: deny access for alleged infringement) are termination for cause, not a TERM-CONV deviation, so not labelled; TERM-CONV left out of scope because Zoom may discontinue the Services at its discretion (c6, tagged ch) while the customer can cancel only to the end of the paid term (c14/c17). GOV-LAW out (California law); DATA-PROT out (external Global DPA incorporated, c29); ASSIGN out (no clause). LANG-PREC left out of scope on review: the rule is for Arabic/English contracts, and this one is English only.

input: Review contract claudette-dropbox and route it.

checks.why: Dropbox limits its liability 'TO THE GREATER OF $20 USD OR 100% OF ANY AMOUNT YOU'VE PAID UNDER YOUR CURRENT SERVICE PLAN' and excludes indirect and business losses (ltd2); nothing caps the customer's liability.
Dropbox bills automatically from the date of conversion and at each periodic renewal, i.e. in advance for the period (fees 'pre-paid', c24/c44); no 30-day invoice term.
Plans renew each billing period until cancellation, with a reminder before an annual renewal (c15); the customer may cancel at any time (c16).
The Terms contain no indemnity from the customer.
